title: Food and Drink
description: Order tea, say you are hungry, and pay a compliment to the cook.

lessons.title: On the table
lessons.goal: Name the everyday foods of a Punjabi kitchen.
notes: roti means both "flatbread" and, loosely, "a meal". roti khani hai? means "do you want to eat?".
dal-roti together is the shorthand for simple home food.

lessons.title: Hungry and thirsty
lessons.goal: Say you are hungry or thirsty and describe a taste.
notes: Hunger "attaches" to you rather than being something you are: mainu bhukkh laggi hai — literally "hunger has struck to me".
bahut means "very" and goes before the adjective: bahut svad — very tasty.

lessons.title: Ordering and refusing
lessons.goal: Ask for what you want, and politely stop the food coming.
notes: chahida changes with the gender of the thing wanted: mainu chah chahidi hai (chah is feminine), mainu pani chahida hai (pani is masculine).
In a Punjabi home you will be offered more food repeatedly. bas ji, said with a smile, is the way out.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.pa: ਹਾਂ ਜੀ, ਮੈਨੂੰ ਚਾਹ ਚਾਹੀਦੀ ਹੈ।
dialogue.roman: han ji, mainu chah chahidi hai.

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.pa: ਰੋਟੀ ਵੀ ਖਾ ਲਵੋ। ਇੱਕ ਹੋਰ?
dialogue.roman: roti vi kha lavo. ikk hor?
dialogue.en: Eat some food too. One more?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.pa: ਬਸ ਜੀ, ਪੇਟ ਭਰ ਗਿਆ। ਬਹੁਤ ਸਵਾਦ ਸੀ।
dialogue.roman: bas ji, pet bhar gaya. bahut svad si.
dialogue.en: That's enough, I'm full. It was very tasty.
